Or do we have just simply incorporate lagged endogenous variable into MIMIC model? Like in here:

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: DYMIMIC model
parts: Is there a way to build DYMIMIC model with "lavaan" package?

Without reading the source, I doubt it.  lavaan considers parameters fixed, so other dynamic models are not possible, neither are models such as MNLFA.  Random intercepts (and eventually slopes) are only possible in the context of MLSEM.  Random-intercept cross-lagged panel models are possible only because data are in wide format.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: DYMIMIC model
parts:
Traditional SEM programs cannot easily addres dynamic model usually.

You can look at parameterizing it as an LDE (latent differencial equation) model from Boker, which adjust it from the growcth curve models

You can look at the ctsem or dynr pacakges.
- ctsem: does dynamic models from the continuous time models based on (stochastic) differential equations models, freuquentis and Bayesian
- dynr: does continous and discrete time dynamic models, based on state space parameterization

messages.subject: Re: DYMIMIC model
parts:
Is DYMIMIC model is just a case of DSEM? 
http://stats.lse.ac.uk/ciraki/framework.pdf:
"The DYMIMIC model of Engle et al. (1985) permits dynamics in the endogenous latent variables but does not allow exogenous latent variables, which facilitated a number of empirical applications in which substantive problems had to be limited to static, perfectly observable exogenous variables."
